# Table&lt;K, V&gt;

The open-addressing table [`HashMap`](/docs/api/collections/hash-map) and [`HashSet`](/docs/api/collections/hash-set) are both built on.

```rux
pub struct Table<K, V> {
    // private fields
}
```

Holds keys, values and one distance byte per slot in three parallel runs. A set instantiates the value type with
something that occupies nothing worth reading, which is what lets one kernel serve both.
Move-only: it owns its storage and entries, prohibits copying, and destroys both with [`~Table`](/docs/api/collections/table#destructor).

## Type parameters

| Name | Description    |
| ---- | -------------- |
| `K`  | the key type   |
| `V`  | the value type |

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>Table</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Table(
    allocator: Allocator,
    seed: TableSeed
) -> Table<K, V>
```

An empty table that has not allocated anything.
`allocator` is borrowed for the call and kept; `seed` is read by value. Costs nothing: a table nothing is put
into never allocates.

| Name        | Type        | Description                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the storage comes from                                      |
| `seed`      | `TableSeed` | the two words that key the hash, which decide the iteration order |

**Returns**: an empty table that has taken no storage yet

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L115)

## Associated functions

<h3 id="capacity-for"><code>CapacityFor</code></h3>

```rux
pub func CapacityFor(length: uint) -> uint ! CollectionError
```

The smallest power-of-two capacity that holds `length` entries without passing the three-quarter load factor.
`length` is read by value. Derived from the entry count rather than from the current capacity, so one rule
covers growing and settling alike.

| Name     | Type   | Description       |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------- |
| `length` | `uint` | how many elements |

**Returns**: the table size that holds that many entries, or `CapacityOverflow` when there is none

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L274)

<h3 id="capacity"><code>Capacity</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Capacity(self: &Table<K, V>) -> uint
```

How many slots the table has.
`self` is borrowed. A power of two, or zero. Not how many entries fit: the load factor keeps a quarter of
them free, because a table run fuller than that spends its time displacing entries rather than storing them.

**Returns**: how many slots it has

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L140)

<h3 id="find"><code>Find</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Find(
    self: &Table<K, V>,
    key: K,
    hash: func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64,
    equals: func(K, K) -> bool
) -> uint?
```

The slot holding `key`, or `none` when the table does not have it.
`self` is borrowed; `key` is read by value; `hash` and `equals` decide identity and must be the same pair the
table was filled with. The seed is handed to `hash`, so a table's hashes are its own.
Stops at the first slot whose occupant is closer to home than the search has travelled: the key would have
displaced that occupant on its way past, so it cannot be further along.
Runs in constant expected time and allocates nothing.

| Name     | Type                                | Description                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `key`    | `K`                                 | the key to look up                                         |
| `hash`   | `func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64` | how a key is hashed, taking the key and the two seed words |
| `equals` | `func(K, K) -> bool`                | whether two keys are the same                              |

**Returns**: the slot the key belongs in, occupied or not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L182)

<h3 id="rehash"><code>Rehash</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Rehash(
    self: &var Table<K, V>,
    capacity: uint,
    hash: func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64
) -> ! CollectionError
```

Rebuilds the table at `capacity` slots, reinserting every entry.
`self` is borrowed mutably; `hash` must be the one the table was filled with. A failure leaves the table
exactly as it was: the new runs are taken and filled before the old ones are released.
Runs in time proportional to the capacity.

| Name       | Type                                | Description                                                |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `capacity` | `uint`                              | how many elements to make room for                         |
| `hash`     | `func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64` | how a key is hashed, taking the key and the two seed words |

**Returns**: nothing when the operation succeeded, or why it did not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L294)

<h3 id="shrink-to-fit"><code>ShrinkToFit</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ShrinkToFit(
    self: &var Table<K, V>,
    hash: func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64
) -> ! CollectionError
```

Releases the capacity the entry count does not need.
`self` is borrowed mutably. An empty table gives up its storage entirely. A failure leaves the table usable
at its current capacity, since failing to hand memory back is never a reason to stop working.

| Name   | Type                                | Description                                                |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hash` | `func(K, uint64, uint64) -> uint64` | how a key is hashed, taking the key and the two seed words |

**Returns**: nothing when the operation succeeded, or why it did not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L377)

## Destructor

```rux
func ~Table(self: &var Table<K, V>)
```

Destroys every entry and releases the storage.
Runs when the table's life ends. The entries go first and the runs second, since one destroyed after its
storage was released would be read from freed memory.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L422)

## Related

<h3 id="slot-empty"><code>SlotEmpty</code></h3>

```rux
pub const SlotEmpty: uint8 = 0;
```

The state byte of a slot that has never held an entry, and does not now.
Distances are stored one higher than they are, so zero can mean empty and nothing else has to.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L30)

<h3 id="maximum-probe-distance"><code>MaximumProbeDistance</code></h3>

```rux
pub const MaximumProbeDistance: uint = 254;
```

The furthest an entry may sit from home before the table gives up and grows.
A byte holds the distance plus one, so 254 is what fits. Reaching it means the hash is doing nothing useful for
these keys, and a table that grew would only spread the same collisions over more slots — so the insertion is
refused rather than looped on.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L37)

<h3 id="minimum-table-capacity"><code>MinimumTableCapacity</code></h3>

```rux
pub const MinimumTableCapacity: uint = 8;
```

Eight slots is where a table starts.
Below that the load factor rounds away to nothing useful.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L42)
